In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the documentation of craftsmanship is not only a matter of recording and archiving.
the documentary record of the old blacksmith's work is not a sufficient resource to learn from.
the documentary is a useful source of knowledge for the blacksmiths, and that the documentary can be improved through a combination of augmented documentation and peer research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
documentation of craft skills should be a collaborative effort between heritage professionals and the craft people themselves.

documentation of craft skills should not be a matter of collecting artefacts or recording the visible and audible, but rather a question of how to elicit the hidden and tacit dimensions of the craft process.
the tacit dimensions are not only to be found in the process, but also in the documentation and the display of the work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the documentation of craft skills should be based on a combination of tacit and explicit knowledge.
the tacit dimension of heritage craft skills can be elicited through a combination of augmented documentation methods and peer re enactment.

documentation and exhibition of traditional crafts should be performed by crafts people, not only to safeguard and transmit the knowledge of the craft, but also to create new knowledge in the craft domain.
